title: Anchoring Recurrent Depth and Exposing Ensemble Blind Spots
subtitle: Sparrow · Ensemble uncertainty · Neural collapse
intro: Main reads connect input injection to truncated backpropagation and explain why ensemble disagreement captures only part of reducible error. A delayed addition covers precision-aware learning-rate transfer; briefs include other new papers, substantive revisions and a proof-RL replication. The classic is Neural Collapse.
window: November 22–25, 2026 (America/New_York; emphasis on updates since the previous issue, with a 72-hour overlap)

articles.paper: How to build and train your recurrent-depth model: A fixed-point perspective
articles.title: Input injection: anchoring, bias and truncated gradients

blocks.text: Reusing shared layers increases inference depth, while training often backpropagates through only the final H steps. The paper identifies persistent injection of fixed input u with Halpern iteration: anchoring helps contraction but also changes the limit. [1]

blocks.label: The paper’s constant-step condition: fixed β can contract even for mildly expansive T. The limit is a fixed point of the anchored operator, generally not of T.

The paper’s truncation bound requires trajectory differentiability, θ-independent u and z⁰, and uniformly B-bounded per-step parameter Jacobians. It is not unbiasedness of arbitrary training gradients.

blocks.text: With nonexpansive T and a nonempty fixed-point set, among other conditions, βₖ=1/log(k+3) removes anchor bias. Absolute gradient error ε needs a window O(log K[log log K+log(1/ε)]). Lipschitz control of the neural parameterization motivates joint row- and spectral-norm constraints. [1]

blocks.label: Sparrow’s cheap feasible direction for jointly constrained parameter groups. Row normalizes each row to radius r; RowClip clips only oversized rows. Spectral is a spectral-ball linear oracle, not spectral clipping. The composition is not the exact joint LMO.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Language experiments mainly use a four-layer, width-128 model on Tiny Shakespeare. No extra overhead is not demonstrated large-scale end-to-end acceleration. Fixed-point/truncation theory does not directly establish global convergence of nonconvex LLM training with Sparrow. [1]

articles.paper: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models
articles.authors: Ravanbakhsh, Siamak · Nitchi, David · Ngo, Khang
articles.title: Ensembles cannot see information all members miss

blocks.text: Let pₓ be the true next-token distribution and qₛ the S members. The paper separates irreducible entropy, reducible error and ensemble-recoverable disagreement through log loss. Agreement does not exhaust epistemic uncertainty. [2]

blocks.label: The paper’s identity needs no model calibration; identifying reducible error with a particular information-theoretic epistemic quantity requires additional calibration conditions.

blocks.tex: q_G(y\mid x)=\frac{\exp\{S^{-1}\sum_s\log q_s(y\mid x)\}}{Z_x},\quad\rho_G=\bar L-L(q_G)=\frac1S\sum_s\mathbb E_XD_{\rm KL}(q_G\|q_s)
blocks.label: The paper’s geometric pooling averages log probabilities and renormalizes. ρG is recovered loss, not all reducible error.
The paper’s visible/invisible decomposition. Their sum is mean-member reducible log loss; shared representation limits can remain in the second term.

blocks.text: On recent text, public-model fits give geometric-spread parameter exponents about 0.118–0.200 versus loss exponents about 0.191–0.313 under a shared-floor assumption. Later branching further reduces diversity. Different decay rates support growing competitiveness with scale, not compute optimality for arbitrary hardware/training budgets. [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Floor estimates, model families, data and pooling affect fits. The S/(S−1) population correction relies on nearby-prediction and independence approximations; it is not an exactly unbiased correction for members sharing training history. [2]

articles.paper: Precision-Aware Learning Rate Transfer Across Block Count in LLM Post-Training
articles.authors: Chen, Nan · Villar, Soledad · Hayou, Soufiane
articles.title: TipSweep: precision changes the depth-transfer exponent

blocks.text: Delayed addition: tune only the final k₀ blocks, then transfer to k trainable blocks. Rates scale approximately as k⁻¹ with FP32 master weights and k⁻¹ᐟ² under direct BF16 updates. Read the PDF abstract and introduction; rounding-model assumptions were not exhaustively audited. There is no single rule across arbitrary precision formats. [3]

articles.paper: Metric-Dependent Scaling Laws for Sketched Multiclass Softmax Regression
articles.authors: Chen, Ziyan · Zheng, Linhe · Liu, Peilin · Zhou, Zhongzhu · Zhou, Ding-Xuan
articles.title: One spectral scale, different risk exponents

blocks.text: In finite-sample-reuse sketched multiclass softmax, cross-entropy excess and excess 0–1 risk share a spectral scale; teacher–student decision disagreement takes its square root. Gaussian teacher–student, spectral and decision-nondegeneracy assumptions matter. Based on abstract and introduction. [4]

articles.paper: InducedTFMs: A Family of Sub-Quadratic Tabular Foundation Models Using Induced Attention
articles.authors: Gobbi, Salome · Atienza, Nicolas · Cancedda, Nicola · Arbel, Michael
articles.title: InducedTFM: complexity versus practical crossover

blocks.text: Both attention stages use induced attention, reducing sample/feature complexity at fixed inducing size. The abstract compares matched training budgets with TabICLv2; inference gains on narrow tables do not imply superiority to row compression on wide tables. [5]

articles.paper: Train What You Run: Probabilistic Convolutions for Learning Token Compaction in State Space Models
articles.authors: Kubaty, Piotr · Saladkou, Mikhail · Tabor, Jacek · Struski, Łukasz
articles.title: ProbConv: account for post-deletion neighborhoods

blocks.text: Under independent keep decisions, the method computes exact expected pre-activation convolution at kept positions and differentiates keep probabilities. Binary decisions reproduce a compacted Mamba block. An expected pre-activation operator is not the expectation of the whole nonlinear network. [6]

articles.title: Robot midtraining: connected behavioral coverage

blocks.text: β-Data uses reversible adversarial perturbations and language relabeling of local outcomes, reporting better data scaling and gains from extra rollout time. Abstract only: behavioral coverage is not the count of successful demonstrations, and no universal exponent is inferred. [7]

articles.paper: MaskedVGGT: Masked Multi-View Transformers Are Scalable 3D Learners
articles.authors: Zou, Zichen · Jia, Xiaosong · Chen, Wen-Ming · Wu, Zuxuan · Jiang, Yu-Gang
articles.title: MaskedVGGT: separate cross-view learning from image representations

blocks.text: A strong 2D encoder is frozen while an added multi-view transformer learns via masked self-distillation from an unmasked EMA teacher. Scaling to 1B and adding unlabeled video provide model/data scaling evidence; equal update counts do not automatically mean equal total FLOPs. [8]

articles.title: Optimizer switching: added stage-wise RLVR comparisons

articles.paper: Learning via Self-Consistency for Diffusion-based Video Reasoning
articles.authors: Ni, Zhenghao · Qiu, Weimin · Tang, Meng
articles.title: Video reasoning: from rejection fine-tuning to self-consistency RL

blocks.text: The earlier version included multi-rollout consensus and rejection fine-tuning. v2 explicitly introduces SC-FT and SC-RL consensus distillation/reward stages to internalize multi-sample gains in one generation. Consensus is not ground truth; removing an external verifier does not prevent reinforcement of shared errors. [13] [14]

articles.paper: FineProofEnvs: Better Math Proofs from a 2B Model with RL
articles.title: Proof-RL replication: rubric scores versus full-proof rates

blocks.text: Qwen3.5-2B trains directly from base with RL on 1,024 problems for 500 steps. Four samples on each of 64 selected held-out problems raise normalized rubric means from 0.217 to 0.407 and full-mark attempts from 12.1% to 25.4%. These are LLM-judge scores, not Lean verification; evaluation problems were filtered for reference-proof gradeability. [15]

classic.title: From zero training error to symmetric classification geometry
classic.paper: Prevalence of neural collapse during the terminal phase of deep learning training
classic.authors: Vardan Papyan · X. Y. Han · David L. Donoho
classic.dateNote: PNAS 2020; first posted August 18, 2020; read v2: August 21, 2020
classic.evidence: Read NC1–NC4 definitions, empirical evidence and relevant arguments

recognition.label: 1,217 citations in the queried OpenAlex record (November 25, 2026)

classic.question: At fixed feature dimension and compute, after making class counts long-tailed, how would you distinguish insufficient optimization, altered class weighting and infeasible simplex geometry?

blocks.text: After training classification error reaches zero, cross-entropy training still changes penultimate representations. Papyan, Han and Donoho (PNAS 2020) organize terminal-phase geometry as Neural Collapse. It is first a collection of empirical phenomena, not a global SGD-convergence theorem for arbitrary networks. [16]

blocks.label: Notation restatement of the paper’s balanced-class setting: C classes and n training features h per class. W measures within-class scatter and B between-class scatter.
A normalized NC1 diagnostic: within-class variability shrinks relative to between-class geometry; feature norms need not vanish.
NC2: centered means approach equal norms and pairwise cosine −1/(C−1), a simplex ETF. Feature dimension must accommodate C−1 dimensions.

NC3 is classifier–centered-mean self-duality. The right identity is an algebraic derivation under ideal equal norms and common bias, explaining NC4’s nearest-class-center rule; it does not guarantee accuracy on arbitrary unseen samples.

blocks.text: The paper tracks post-zero-error training geometry across datasets, networks and loss settings. Within-class collapse, simplex ETF geometry, self-duality and NCC decisions should be tested separately; one nearly satisfied diagnostic does not imply all four. [16]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Read definitions, empirical evidence and relevant arguments; experiments not reproduced. Balanced classes, sufficient feature dimension and terminal training regime matter. Regular training geometry does not automatically explain test generalization or tail-class performance. [16]
